title: Meerkats Catalog Resolved Plan v1 — the semantic-catalog layer's output contract
description: The JSON the catalog resolver (meerkats-catalog resolve.mjs) hands back for a routed task — the interface between the semantic-catalog (RDF) layer and everything that consumes it (agent planners, the service, evidence queries). Field names are exactly the resolver's; nothing here invents vocabulary. The graph side of this layer is contracted separately: shapes.ttl (SHACL) governs the TTL, verify.py proves catalog.json ≡ TTL; THIS schema governs what crosses the layer boundary at question time. Honesty rules are structural: resolved:true requires at least one plan and an empty unresolved; resolved:false requires no plans and at least one stated reason; a non-fanout response carries at most one plan and an empty not_available_on. A refusal is a success, not a failure — it must arrive as unresolved[] entries with a why, never as a silent empty response.

build_id.description: hash of all four build inputs — says exactly which catalog produced this plan

fanout.description: true when a platform-less request was split into per-platform plans (e.g. product = advertised_asin on amazon, fsn_id on flipkart)

plans.description: always an array — one entry for a normal query, several when fanned out — so the consumer has a single shape to handle

not_available_on.description: fanout only: platforms that cannot answer at this grain, each with the stated reason

id.description: caveat key in the catalog (e.g. fanout_not_totalled)

caveats.description: things that change how the result must be read; blocker caveats must surface with the answer

note.description: binding note, e.g. why a substitute metric was chosen

kind.description: bug: catalog/request defect. parked: recognised, data not ingested. refusal: correctly unanswerable, reason stated. broken: metric's model references a missing column

unresolved.description: non-empty means the task fails BEFORE any generation is paid for — with reasons, never silently

plan.description: One executable metric plan: which MetricFlow metric to call, on which semantic model, grouped by what. The consumer executes this verbatim — it never re-chooses a metric.

asked.description: the word the task said (roas, roi, spend…)

use.description: the MetricFlow metric to actually call

why.description: stated when use ≠ the obvious mapping (e.g. platform_reported_roas because roas is cross-model)

time_asked.description: true when the task asked for the time dimension itself

allOf.description: a resolved response must carry at least one plan and no unresolved entries
an unresolved response must carry no plans and at least one stated reason
a non-fanout response has at most one plan and nothing in not_available_on
